problem.summary: 现有区域丢弃（regional dropout）数据增强方法（如Cutout）通过覆盖黑色像素或随机噪声来移除图像区域，导致信息丢失和训练效率低下。

motivation.summary: 如何在保留区域丢弃带来的正则化效果（引导模型关注物体非判别性部分）的同时，最大化利用被丢弃区域的信息，从而提高训练效率和模型性能。

core_idea.summary: 提出CutMix增强策略：从训练图像中剪切出图像块并粘贴到另一张图像上，同时按图像块面积比例混合两张图像的标签。这既保留了区域丢弃的正则化效果，又避免了信息丢失，使训练更高效。

method.summary: CutMix算法：1) 从Beta分布Beta(α,α)采样混合比例λ；2) 采样裁剪框坐标B=(rx, ry, rw, rh)，其中rw=W√(1-λ)，rh=H√(1-λ)；3) 生成二值掩码M；4) 按公式˜x = M⊙xA + (1−M)⊙xB混合图像，˜y = λyA + (1−λ)yB混合标签。

experiments.summary: 在CIFAR-100、ImageNet分类、ImageNet弱监督定位、Pascal VOC检测、MS-COCO图像描述等多个任务和数据集上进行了广泛实验，与Cutout、Mixup等基线方法进行了比较。

claims.claim: CutMix在分类、定位、检测、描述等多个任务上一致优于现有增强策略；能提高模型对输入损坏和对抗攻击的鲁棒性；能改善分布外检测性能；作为预训练模型能提升下游任务性能。

limitations.limitation: 论文未明确讨论CutMix在极端数据不平衡或小数据集上的效果；未详细分析其对不同网络架构的敏感性；未探讨其与其它正则化技术（如Dropout）的交互作用。

metadata.title: CutMix: Regularization Strategy to Train Strong Classifiers With Localizable Features
metadata.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
metadata.paper_type: Computer Vision / Pose Estimation / Vision-Language / Captioning / Computer Vision / CNN / Computer Vision / Top-cited Computer Vision paper
metadata.abstract: Regional dropout strategies have been proposed to enhance performance of convolutional neural network classifiers. They have proved to be effective for guiding the model to attend on less discriminative parts of objects (e.g. leg as opposed to head of a person), thereby letting the network generalize better and have better object localization capabilities. On the other hand, current methods for regional dropout removes informative pixels on training images by overlaying a patch of either black pixels or random noise. Such removal is not desirable because it suffers from information loss causing inefficiency in training. We therefore propose the CutMix augmentation strategy: patches are cut and pasted among training images where the ground truth labels are also mixed proportionally to the area of the patches. By making efficient use of training pixels and retaining the regularization effect of regional dropout, CutMix consistently outperforms state-of-the-art augmentation strategies on CIFAR and ImageNet classification tasks, as well as on ImageNet weakly-supervised localization task. Moreover, unlike previous augmentation methods, our CutMix-trained ImageNet classifier, when used as a pretrained model, results in consistent performance gain in Pascal detection and MS-COCO image captioning benchmarks. We also show that CutMix can improve the model robustness against input corruptions and its out-of-distribution detection performance.
